description: One Moon is one week. Each Moon favours one errand by a single point; everything else about it is narrative. The tie-in lines are woven into the Dawn Report for whatever the warband actually did that night. Slots: {first} the member's first name, {district} where they went.

moons.name: Plague Moon
moons.reading: Chalk on the doors. The Sisters do not sleep.

ties.scavenge: The rubble in {district} had been picked over by people who did not come back for the rest.
ties.carouse: Half the tavern wore cloth over their faces. The other half had stopped caring.
ties.train: The Pit ran short-handed. Two of the regulars are under chalk.
ties.spy: Every second door {first} passed was marked. Nobody spoke above a whisper.
ties.pray: The Sisters had run out of candles by the third hour and kept praying in the dark.
ties.trade: Henrik weighed the coin through a cloth and did not touch it.

moons.name: Hunter's Moon
moons.reading: Wide hats in every doorway. Nobody drinks. Nobody trades.

ties.scavenge: A wide hat watched from the end of the street the whole time.
ties.carouse: The tavern went quiet twice. Both times a hat had come in.
ties.train: The Pit was the one place the hunters left alone. It was full.
ties.spy: {first} was not the only one listening. The other one had a torch.
ties.pray: A witch hunter knelt in the front row of the shrine. Nobody knelt near him.
ties.trade: Henrik's shutters were down. The deal was done through the letterbox.

moons.name: Green Moon
moons.reading: The comet flares. The rubble hums.

ties.scavenge: The rubble hummed under {first}'s hands. Nobody stopped to wonder why.
ties.carouse: The ale had a green cast to it by candlelight. Nobody sent it back.
ties.train: The comet's light came through the roof of the Pit. Every shadow had two edges.
ties.spy: The whole quarter glowed faintly. It made the listening easier and the hiding worse.
ties.pray: The candle flames burned green for a moment. The Sisters did not comment.
ties.trade: Henrik's scale would not settle. He blamed the moon.

moons.name: Festival of Hanging
moons.reading: The gibbets are full and so are the taverns.

ties.scavenge: The crowds were all at the gibbets. {first} had {district} alone.
ties.carouse: The whole city was drinking to the hanged. {first} drank to them twice.
ties.train: The Pit drew the overflow from the gibbets. They wanted more of what they had seen.
ties.spy: Everyone was talking. It was hard to hear anything for the talk.
ties.pray: The Sisters were saying the rites for the hanged. {first} waited a long time for a candle.
ties.trade: The fences did brisk business in the effects of the dead.

moons.name: Silent Moon
moons.reading: No bells. No carts. Whoever is listening has stopped.

ties.scavenge: No bells, no carts. {first} could hear each stone fall.
ties.carouse: The tavern spoke in murmurs. Even the dice were quiet.
ties.train: The Pit fought without a crowd. The blows sounded louder for it.
ties.spy: In the silence every word carried three streets.
ties.pray: Nobody sang. The candles did what candles do.
ties.trade: Henrik wrote his price on a slate and turned it around.

moons.name: Market Moon
moons.reading: Barges on the Stir. Every fence has two prices and both are good.

ties.scavenge: Barge crews were already picking at the shoreline ruins.
ties.carouse: The tavern was full of sailors with coin and no sense of how much.
ties.train: Boatmen wagered on the Pit with the day's wages. The purse was fat.
ties.spy: The docks were loud with strangers. Strangers talk.
ties.pray: The Sisters took a collection at the door. It was a good night for it.
ties.trade: There were three buyers for every sliver and Henrik hated all of them.

moons.name: Ash Moon
moons.reading: The wind is from the west. The streets rewrite themselves.

ties.scavenge: The wind had moved the ash overnight. Streets were there that had not been.
ties.carouse: Ash came in under the tavern door and settled on the ale. Nobody minded.
ties.train: The Pit's sand was grey by the second bout.
ties.spy: Footprints in the ash told {first} who had passed, and how many.
ties.pray: The candles guttered in the draught and had to be relit twice.
ties.trade: Henrik wiped ash from the scale between every weighing.

moons.name: Debtor's Moon
moons.reading: Old Henrik is calling in what he is owed. So is everyone else.

ties.scavenge: Someone had been through {district} already, in a hurry, owing money.
ties.carouse: Every table in the tavern was arguing about who owed whom.
ties.train: The Pit's purse was small. Half of it had been claimed before the first bout.
ties.spy: Debt makes people talk. {first} let them.
ties.pray: The shrine's poor box had been forced. The Sisters prayed for whoever did it.
ties.trade: Henrik was calling in what he was owed and paid quickly to be rid of the coin.
